newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end at record high.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end at record high.

text.p: Swiss shares closed at a record high after overcoming a moment of weakness following the release of U.S. Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data.
The indices broke new ground, continuing their recent record run. The fact that U.S. shares held up well in early trade also helped the Swiss market, dealers said.

U.S. GDP expanded at a 5.6 percent annual rate in the first three months of this year following a 3.8 percent rate of growth in last year's final quarter. Wall Street economists had forecast a 4.1 percent growth rate.

The Swiss Market Index gained 42.5 points, or 0.88 percent, to close at 4,897.6 after hitting an intraday high of 4,903.5. The Swiss Performance Index rose 23.70 points, or 0.77 percent, to finish at 3,094.65.
Total bourse turnover was 2.51 billion francs.
Despite the gains there was still some uncertainty in the market since U.S. markets will be open on Thursday but the Swiss bourse closed for the Labour Day holiday, one dealer said.
UBS bearer shares were in the limelight during today's session. The rise of nine francs to 1,395 mainly stemmed from buy recommendations, one trader said.
SBC also gained strength. CS Group lost 0.75 francs to end at 166.0.

Major insurers showed a strong performance, especially Zurich, which gained nine francs, or nearly two percent, to end at 484.0. After the bourse closed Zurich said its 1996 net profit rose 0.2 percent to 1,138.2 million francs.
Among major pharmaceuticals, Novartis registered shares were the winner on the day, advancing 28 francs to 1,942. Roche certificates were up 95 to 12,450.
ABB, Holderbank and SMH were up around one percent each. Swissair slid 22 to 1,290. Adecco was up 12 to 492 after reporting first quarter results.
